LanguageData.AT_AutoManned: Manned turrets fire on their own
LanguageData.AT_AutoManned_Desc: Your turrets that normally need a colonist (from any mod) shoot automatically, like a mini-turret. You can still pick a target by hand.
LanguageData.AT_AutoMortars_Desc: Your mortars and other shell weapons shoot at enemies automatically while they have a shell loaded.
LanguageData.AT_MortarSafety: Mortars don't shoot near your people
LanguageData.AT_MortarSafety_Desc: An automatic mortar skips targets where the shell could land on your colonists, animals or guests.
LanguageData.AT_LoadShells_Desc: Haulers carry shells from anywhere on the map to automatic mortars that are empty. The mortar's own shell filter is respected.
LanguageData.AT_AnyMetal_Desc: Turrets that rearm with steel (or another single metal) take any metal: steel, plasteel, gold, uranium and metals from mods.
LanguageData.AT_Restart: Material and wall turret settings apply after restarting the game.
LanguageData.AT_FriendlyFire_Desc: When off, bullets from your turrets fly past your colonists, guests and allies, and blasts from their shells don't hurt them. On = like the game.
LanguageData.AT_FuelWood: Turrets can be refilled with wood
LanguageData.AT_FuelWood_Desc: Turrets that rearm with metal also take wood.
LanguageData.AT_FuelStone: Turrets can be refilled with stone blocks
LanguageData.AT_FuelStone_Desc: Turrets that rearm with metal also take stone blocks.
LanguageData.AT_WallTurrets_Desc: Picked turrets get a second version "… (in wall)" in the Security menu. It is built straight over a wall or a smoothed rock wall, replaces that piece of wall and works as a wall itself: it blocks the way, holds the roof and keeps the room sealed. The normal turrets stay as they are.
LanguageData.AT_WallDescExtra: Built over a wall: it looks like a piece of that wall (in its material) with the gun on top, joins the walls next to it, blocks the way and holds the roof. Small 1×1 turrets cost 5 extra of the wall material. If it is destroyed, a hole is left in the wall.
LanguageData.AT_WallRecDone: Recommended selection restored – {0} small turrets selected.
LanguageData.AT_RestartNeeded: ⚠ Restart the game for the wall turret changes to apply.
LanguageData.AT_SmartShells_Desc: Automatic mortars don't waste shells: EMP only at mechanoids and shielded enemies, incendiary not at mechanoids, firefoam only at fires in the home area (never at enemies). Haulers bring EMP shells when most enemies are mechanoids, otherwise high-explosive ones – if the mortar's filter allows them.
LanguageData.AT_NoHitBuildings_Desc: When on, bullets from your turrets fly past your own buildings (walls, sandbags, doors…) unless you aimed at them, and blasts from their shells don't damage them. Enemy buildings are hit as usual. Off = like the game.
LanguageData.AT_WallOutward_Desc: A turret in a wall only shoots at targets on the outer side of its wall (away from the room). If neither side is clearly outside (a wall between two rooms), it shoots everywhere.
LanguageData.AT_TurretsDesc: Every turret, mortar and gun – vanilla and from mods. Ticked ones fire on their own. Unticked: manned turrets and mortars need a colonist again, automatic turrets hold fire until you pick a target.
LanguageData.AT_FuelPerTurret: Each turret's materials – also turrets that need their own ammo or fuel from a mod. Click "Materials…" and tick what else it may be rearmed with. Changes work right away.
LanguageData.AT_FuelOriginal: Takes by itself: {0}. Tick what else it may be rearmed with:
LanguageData.AT_GizmoAutoLoad_Desc: Haulers bring shells to this mortar by themselves. Turn off to load it only by hand.
LanguageData.AT_GizmoAmmo_Desc: Pick the one shell or material this turret is loaded or rearmed with – nothing else is brought. "Anything allowed" uses everything the turret takes.
LanguageData.AT_SpecialOnlyPicked_Desc: Haulers bring EMP, incendiary, firefoam and other special shells only to a mortar set to them with its "Ammo" button; otherwise they bring high-explosive shells.
LanguageData.AT_AmmoAlsoMetal: Turrets with their own ammo take any metal too
LanguageData.AT_AmmoAlsoMetal_Desc: Turrets that need their own ammo or fuel (often from mods) can also be rearmed with steel or any other metal – so they never stand idle because their ammo is missing.
LanguageData.AT_FreeAmmo_Desc: Your turrets always count as loaded and never use up ammo or fuel. Useful when a mod's turret needs ammo you can't make. Mortars, artillery and field guns always have a shell loaded too.
LanguageData.AT_VfesAuto: Fires by itself (Auto Turrets) – no colonist needed.
LanguageData.AT_VfesSend: Nobody mans it – the nearest free colonist who can fight goes there right away.
LanguageData.AT_ShellsFromMaterial: Load mortars and artillery with material instead of shells
LanguageData.AT_ShellsFromMaterial_Desc: Haulers bring steel (or another metal) to mortars, artillery and field guns and the gun is loaded with the shell you picked for it, otherwise a high-explosive one. Shells are not needed at all. The VFE automated mortar refills its shells from material too.
LanguageData.AT_NoMaterial: Not enough material ({0} metal per shell)
LanguageData.AT_StunRunaways: Stun turrets stop escaping prisoners and slaves
LanguageData.AT_StunRunaways_Desc: Your stunning (non-lethal) turrets also shoot at your prisoners and slaves who break out, rebel, flee or go berserk. Lethal turrets still leave them alone.
LanguageData.AT_StunGiveUp_Desc: A prisoner breaking out or a slave rebelling who is stunned or downed by your turret gives up: wardens take him back to his cell, a slave goes back to work.
LanguageData.AT_GaveUpPrisoner: {0} was stunned and gave up the escape.
LanguageData.AT_GaveUpSlave: {0} was stunned and gave up the rebellion.
LanguageData.AT_ShellDestroyed: Your artillery has destroyed {0}. The people of {1} left the ruins.
LanguageData.AT_ShellApplied: Your artillery hit {0} {1} times before you came – the shells fell on it now.
LanguageData.AT_ShellStart: Artillery shells {0} – about {1} more hits destroy it.
LanguageData.AT_ShellSettlements: Artillery shells hostile bases without a map
LanguageData.AT_ShellSettlements_Desc: VFE Security world artillery can fire at a hostile base you have not visited. Each hit is counted: when you attack the base, the hits fall on it first (fewer defenders), and enough hits destroy it.
LanguageData.AT_ShellHitsN: Hits that destroy a base: {0} (fewer for tribes, more for spacers)
LanguageData.AT_ShellNotHostile: {0} ({1}) is not hostile – artillery shells only hostile bases (or a map you have open).
LanguageData.AT_ShellNoTarget: Here is nothing to shell. Pick a hostile base (it does not need to be explored) or a map you have open.
